That completes every behaviour you raised — 8 further flows explored and settled on top of the original four. Here's the full picture of what's now locked down, in plain terms:

**Saving**
- Paste a link; its **title, description, icon and preview image** are fetched automatically and are editable. Save even when a page can't be reached; incomplete links are flagged; pasting a link you already saved opens it for editing instead of duplicating.
- **Tags** with suggestions from tags you already use (with usage counts), and a **note** supporting simple Markdown with a live preview.
- A **preserved copy** is kept by default (the PDF itself for PDFs), with an optional Internet Archive copy.

**Organising**
- **To read / Done / Archived**, where archiving is separate from read status and restoring returns a link to where it was. Edit and permanent delete.
- **Bulk actions** on a selection, a page, or everything matching a view/search: tag/untag, mark read/unread, archive, delete.

**Finding**
- Per-view **search** across title, link, description and note (case-insensitive), with a query language (`#tags`, `"phrases"`, `and`/`or`/`not`, parentheses), click-a-tag filtering, and **named saved searches**.

**Living with a big collection**
- **Sort** (date added / title), **page size** (10/25/50), paging, and a **text size** preference — all remembered.
- **Import and export** in the standard bookmark HTML format, preserving titles, tags, and original dates.

All of it **private to you and persisting between visits**. One thing still explicitly deferred: the favicon/preview image are the only place we relied on a *simulated* stand-in; in the real app they'd be genuinely fetched.

**May I now switch from exploring to building this as the real application?** I'll only make the change once you say yes.
